Procedure_Name: 3-Year & LTM Income Statement Growth & Common-Sizing Analysis
Analytical_Objective: Establish multi-year compound growth rates and baseline cost structure dynamics across all P&L lines.
Financial_Question_Investigated: Is the company experiencing genuine operational expansion or is growth masking underlying cost inflation?
Source_Data_Required: SRC-001 (Prepared TBs), SRC-003 (Monthly Mgmt Accounts), REC-001 to REC-003 (Reconciled P&L)
Periods_Covered: 3 Historical Fiscal Years (FY21, FY22, FY23) plus LTM
Entities_Covered: Consolidated Group and individual operating subsidiaries
Analytical_Method: Compound Annual Growth Rate (CAGR), Year-over-Year (YoY) percentage change, Vertical Common-Size (% of Revenue).
Detailed_Procedure: Calculate YoY growth: (Year_t - Year_t-1) / Year_t-1; calculate 2-year CAGR: (Year_t / Year_t-2)^(1/2) - 1; express every expense line as a percentage of gross revenue; compute margin percentage deltas.
Metrics_Produced: Revenue CAGR, Gross Profit CAGR, EBITDA CAGR, Common-size % for COGS, S&M, G&A, D&A, and EBITDA.
Common_Findings_Patterns: Revenue expands while gross margin contracts; operating expenses grow faster than revenue, indicating negative operating leverage.
Potential_Distortions: Revenue pulled forward via aggressive year-end cut-offs; reclassifications between COGS and operating expenses across fiscal years.
Further_Investigative_Questions: Did price increases match unit inflation? Were new corporate overhead functions added? Were one-time transaction fees included in G&A?
Required_Evidence: EVD-001 (Audited financials), EVD-005 (Sales registers), EVD-010 (Payroll records)
Downstream_Dependencies: WS05 (EBITDA Normalization for non-operating overhead spikes)
Source_References: PwC TAS Manual; CFA Institute Financial Statement Analysis

Analytical_Objective: Decompose historical top-line revenue growth into discrete price, sales volume, and product mix effects.
Financial_Question_Investigated: Was historical revenue growth driven by underlying customer demand (volume) or inflationary price pass-throughs?
Source_Data_Required: SRC-006 (Detailed Sales Register / Invoices), SRC-010 (Product Master / SKU Catalog)
Periods_Covered: Annual comparison (FY22 vs FY23) and LTM vs Prior LTM
Entities_Covered: By product category, SKU family, and business unit
Analytical_Method: Mathematical 3-bucket variance decomposition holding volume, price, and mix constant.
Detailed_Procedure: Compute Price Effect = (P1 - P0) * V1; compute Volume Effect = (V1 - V0) * P0; compute Mix Effect = (Total_V1 * Sum(Mix1_i * P0_i) - Total_V1 * P0_bar); reconcile sum of components to total dollar revenue change.
Metrics_Produced: Dollar Price Effect, Dollar Volume Effect, Dollar Mix Effect, Percentage contribution to total revenue growth.
Common_Findings_Patterns: Growth is overwhelmingly driven by price hikes with stagnant or declining physical unit volume; mix shift toward lower-margin commodity products.
Potential_Distortions: Inconsistent units of measure across SKUs; customer rebates or retroactive discounts netted against price rather than isolated.
Further_Investigative_Questions: Can the company continue passing cost inflation to customers without destroying volume? Are price increases contractual or ad-hoc?
Required_Evidence: EVD-005 (Transactional customer invoices with units, item master pricing sheets)
Relevant_Business_Models: Distribution/Wholesale, Manufacturing (Adapted for SaaS via ARPU/Seats)
Source_References: FTI Consulting Commercial Diligence; DataMa PVM Framework

Procedure_Name: Gross Margin Bridge & Input Cost Inflation Analysis
Analytical_Objective: Isolate the fundamental drivers of gross margin expansion or compression across product categories.
Financial_Question_Investigated: Why did gross margin deteriorate by 171 bps between FY21 and FY23 despite record sales growth?
Source_Data_Required: SRC-001 (TB COGS accounts), SRC-008 (AP invoices for raw materials), SRC-010 (SKU margin reports)
Periods_Covered: Monthly and annual across 3 historical years (FY21, FY22, FY23)
Entities_Covered: Operating entities with physical manufacturing or distribution operations
Analytical_Method: Gross margin rate variance analysis; component cost percentage roll-forward (Raw Materials % vs Labor % vs Freight %).
Detailed_Procedure: Calculate Gross Margin % = Gross Profit / Revenue; compute Component Ratio = Cost_Category / Revenue; bridge basis point changes from FY21 to FY23; identify if compression is structural or temporary.
Metrics_Produced: Gross Margin % by year, Basis point margin bridge, Component cost percentages (Material %, Labor %, Freight %).
Common_Findings_Patterns: Raw material steel and resin costs increased 17% in FY23; client delayed customer price surcharges by 5 months, absorbing margin compression.
Potential_Distortions: Lower-of-cost-or-market inventory obsolescence write-downs buried in COGS; standard cost variance adjustments booked as lump sums at year-end.
Further_Investigative_Questions: What is the contractual lag for passing raw material price increases to customers? Are key commodity contracts hedged or index-linked?
Required_Evidence: EVD-007 (Vendor raw material price indices), EVD-008 (Perpetual inventory stock valuation reports)
Expected_Analytical_Output: ANA-003 (Gross Margin Bridge & Cost Component Workpaper)
Downstream_Dependencies: WS05 (Normalization of unabsorbed temporary input cost spikes)
Source_References: Alvarez & Marsal TAS Methodology; US GAAP ASC 330

Procedure_Name: Direct Labor Efficiency & Overtime Trend Analysis
Analytical_Objective: Evaluate the productivity, wage inflation, and overtime reliance of direct shop floor manufacturing labor.
Financial_Question_Investigated: Did direct labor costs rise disproportionately due to wage rate inflation or plant operational inefficiencies?
Source_Data_Required: SRC-014 (Payroll Registers / Timecard Systems), SRC-021 (Job Costing / Work Order Labor Logs)
Periods_Covered: Monthly for 24 months across operating plants
Analytical_Method: Direct labor cost per standard hour, overtime % of total hours, labor productivity ratio (Revenue / Direct Labor $).
Detailed_Procedure: Extract direct labor hours and dollars; calculate Average Hourly Direct Labor Rate = Direct Labor $ / Total Labor Hours; calculate Overtime Ratio = Overtime Hours / Total Hours; compare trend against production output.
Metrics_Produced: Average Hourly Rate ($/hr), Overtime % of Labor, Direct Labor % of Revenue, Production Units per Labor Hour.
Common_Findings_Patterns: Overtime surged from 6.2% of hours in FY21 to 14.8% in FY23; skilled machinist turnover forced plant to run excessive weekend shifts at 1.5x pay.
Potential_Distortions: Temporary contract agency labor booked in SG&A consulting rather than direct COGS labor; labor capitalized into WIP inventory.
Further_Investigative_Questions: What is the union or collective bargaining contract status? What is the voluntary employee turnover rate on the shop floor?
Required_Evidence: EVD-010 (Shop floor timecard extracts, payroll tax filings, agency temp staffing invoices)
Downstream_Dependencies: WS05 (Normalization of excessive non-recurring overtime due to plant moves)
Source_References: AICPA Audit Guide for Manufacturing; Kroll Operations Practice

Procedure_Name: Manufacturing Factory Overhead Absorption & Costing Analysis
Analytical_Objective: Analyze how fixed and variable plant overhead is absorbed into inventory and detect volume-driven margin distortion.
Financial_Question_Investigated: Did high production volumes in Q3-Q4 artificially depress COGS by over-absorbing fixed overhead into inventory?
Source_Data_Required: SRC-022 (Factory Overhead Cost Ledgers), SRC-010 (Perpetual Inventory WIP/FG Ledgers)
Periods_Covered: Monthly and annual for 3 historical years
Entities_Covered: All manufacturing plants and production facilities
Analytical_Method: Standard overhead absorption rate comparison against actual incurred plant overhead; variance tracking.
Detailed_Procedure: Calculate Standard Overhead Rate = Budgeted Overhead / Budgeted Machine Hours; compute Applied Overhead = Standard Rate * Actual Hours; calculate Absorption Variance = Actual Overhead Incurred - Applied Overhead; evaluate year-end P&L release.
Metrics_Produced: Actual Overhead Incurred, Applied Overhead, Over/Under-Absorption Variance ($), Overhead Absorption % of Actual.
Common_Findings_Patterns: Plant ran machine lines at 110% capacity in Q4, creating  of over-absorbed overhead credited to COGS, masking margin deterioration.
Potential_Distortions: Overhead absorption formulas changed mid-year without disclosing policy shift; SG&A corporate costs allocated to plant overhead.
Further_Investigative_Questions: What was the plant capacity utilization percentage by month? How were production volume variances treated at fiscal year-end?
Required_Evidence: EVD-016 (Plant production run tickets, standard cost BOM cards, actual factory overhead ledgers)
Downstream_Dependencies: WS05 (Normalization of unearned gross margin lift from inventory over-absorption)
Source_References: US GAAP ASC 330; EY TAS Operations Diligence Guide

Procedure_Name: SG&A Operating Leverage & Fixed vs. Variable Cost Decomposition
Analytical_Objective: Decompose operating expenses into fixed, variable, and step-fixed costs to evaluate operating leverage.
Financial_Question_Investigated: How will operating profitability behave if revenue contracts by 10% or expands by 20% post-acquisition?
Source_Data_Required: SRC-001 (TB Opex accounts), SRC-002 (GL Detail descriptions), SRC-003 (Monthly Mgmt accounts)
Periods_Covered: Monthly and annual for 3 historical years (FY21-FY23) and LTM
Entities_Covered: Consolidated group and administrative shared services
Analytical_Method: Regression / scatter-plot cost behavior analysis; variable expense ratio; fixed cost run-rate calculation.
Detailed_Procedure: Classify each SG&A account as Fixed (rent, executive base pay, insurance), Variable (sales commissions, freight-out), or Step-Fixed (IT software licenses, customer support reps); calculate Degree of Operating Leverage (DOL) = % Change in EBIT / % Change in Revenue.
Metrics_Produced: Fixed SG&A $ run-rate, Variable SG&A % of revenue, Degree of Operating Leverage (DOL), Breakeven revenue threshold.
Common_Findings_Patterns: Operating leverage stalled in FY23; SG&A grew 16.6% while revenue grew 14.0% (DOL = 0.85), driven by aggressive corporate overhead hiring.
Potential_Distortions: One-off transaction, litigation, or restructuring expenses buried in recurring legal and professional fee accounts.
Further_Investigative_Questions: Which SG&A costs are strictly required for standalone operations? What corporate shared service costs will be stranded post-close?
Required_Evidence: EVD-002 (Management close decks), EVD-010 (Executive contracts), EVD-011 (Facility lease agreements)
Expected_Analytical_Output: ANA-006 (SG&A Cost Behavior & Operating Leverage Workpaper)
Downstream_Dependencies: WS05 (Stand-alone cost adjustments and non-recurring opex add-backs)
Source_References: Houlihan Lokey TAS Guide; CFA Institute Corporate Finance

Analytical_Objective: Examine historical headcount, compensation per employee, sales productivity, and incentive bonus structures.
Financial_Question_Investigated: Has wage inflation and headcount growth outpaced revenue generation, and are key executives under-compensated relative to market?
Source_Data_Required: SRC-014 (Detailed Employee Census), SRC-015 (Form 941 / W-2 Summaries), SRC-001 (TB Payroll Accounts)
Periods_Covered: Quarterly and annual for 3 historical years
Entities_Covered: All operating entities and corporate departments (S&M, R&D, G&A, Operations)
Analytical_Method: Headcount roll-forward (Beg + Hires - Terminations = End); Revenue per Head; Average Compensation per Employee.
Detailed_Procedure: Reconcile employee census headcount by department; calculate Average Base Pay and Total Compensation per FTE; compute Revenue per Employee = Revenue / Average Headcount; evaluate historical bonus achievement percentages.
Metrics_Produced: Ending FTE Headcount, Average Compensation per FTE ($), Revenue per Employee ($), Bonus as % of Base Pay.
Common_Findings_Patterns: Headcount increased 22% in FY23 while revenue increased 14%; revenue per employee declined from  to ; executive base pay is 30% below market.
Potential_Distortions: Severance payments or signing bonuses lumped into regular base wages; contractor headcount excluded from official census.
Further_Investigative_Questions: What will it cost to replace selling shareholders post-close at fair market compensation? Are historical bonuses discretionary or formulaic?
Required_Evidence: EVD-010 (Full employee census with job titles, base pay, bonus history, and hire dates)
Downstream_Dependencies: WS05 (Pro-forma market compensation adjustments for selling owners)
Source_References: BDO Transaction Advisory Services; Mercer Compensation Benchmarks

Procedure_Name: Operating EBITDA & Margin Compression / Expansion Bridge
Analytical_Objective: Construct a multi-year bridge showing the precise operational dollar contributions to EBITDA changes.
Financial_Question_Investigated: What specific commercial, cost, and operational factors explain why EBITDA only grew ,000 in FY23 despite .05M of revenue growth?
Source_Data_Required: ANA-001 (Income Statement Trends), ANA-002 (PVM Bridge), ANA-003 (Gross Margin Bridge)
Periods_Covered: Annual comparison (FY21 to FY22, FY22 to FY23) and LTM vs Prior LTM
Entities_Covered: Consolidated group and core operating divisions
Analytical_Method: Waterfall bridge decomposition: Starting EBITDA + Revenue Growth Contribution + Margin Impact - SG&A Expansion = Ending EBITDA.
Detailed_Procedure: Calculate Gross Profit Contribution from Volume = Delta_Volume * Prior_Gross_Margin; calculate Price vs Cost Impact = Delta_Price - Delta_Input_Costs; subtract Incremental SG&A Costs; reconcile to actual reported EBITDA change.
Metrics_Produced: Waterfall bridge components ($), Gross Margin contribution ($), Opex drag ($), Net EBITDA delta ($).
Common_Findings_Patterns: In FY23, .16M of gross profit from revenue expansion was almost entirely wiped out by  of SG&A cost inflation and  of unrecovered raw material price increases.
Potential_Distortions: Management presenting add-backs inside reported EBITDA rather than as a separate bridge to adjusted EBITDA.
Further_Investigative_Questions: Which cost increases are permanent structural investments vs temporary operational friction? Why did pricing lag material inflation?
Required_Evidence: EVD-001 (Audited financials), EVD-002 (CFO month-end files), EVD-007 (Vendor invoices)
Downstream_Dependencies: WS05 (Foundational baseline bridge to Normalized EBITDA)
Source_References: PwC Quality of Earnings Handbook; RSM Financial Due Diligence

Procedure_Name: Monthly & Quarterly Seasonality & Quarter-End Hockey-Stick Analysis
Analytical_Objective: Analyze monthly financial volatility, seasonal working capital cycles, and detect period-end revenue acceleration.
Financial_Question_Investigated: Does the company display genuine seasonal peaks, or do quarter-end months spike artificially due to aggressive closing practices?
Source_Data_Required: SRC-003 (Monthly Management Accounts - 36 Months), SRC-006 (Monthly Sales Registers)
Entities_Covered: Consolidated Group and primary operating subsidiaries
Analytical_Method: Monthly index calculation (Month / Average Month); quarter-end shipping concentration ratio; monthly margin variance.
Detailed_Procedure: Calculate monthly revenue share of annual total; compare Month 3 of each quarter (March, June, September, December) against Months 1 and 2; test for quarter-end hockey stick revenue spikes; evaluate whether gross margins drop in quarter-end months due to heavy discounting.
Metrics_Produced: Monthly Seasonal Indices (0.8x to 1.3x), Quarter-end concentration %, Monthly Gross Margin volatility standard deviation.
Common_Findings_Patterns: December routinely represents 10-11% of annual revenue and 14-16% of EBITDA; quarter-end months exhibit significant revenue acceleration followed by January sales drops.
Potential_Distortions: Year-end accounting catch-up adjustments (annual bonuses, inventory write-downs) posted in December distorting normal monthly run-rate.
Further_Investigative_Questions: Are quarter-end spikes supported by real customer demand or customer channel-stuffing and extended payment terms?
Required_Evidence: EVD-005 (Monthly sales registers, customer shipping dates), EVD-009 (Monthly bank statements)
Downstream_Dependencies: WS06 (Revenue Quality & Cut-Off Testing), WS07 (Seasonal Working Capital Peg)
Source_References: Grant Thornton Due Diligence Guide; Bessemer Private Equity Analytics

Procedure_Name: Customer & Product Line Revenue Concentration & Margin Tiering
Analytical_Objective: Evaluate revenue and gross profit concentration across the top 10/20 customers and product lines.
Financial_Question_Investigated: What percentage of gross profit is dependent on the top 5 customers, and are the largest customers generating sub-par margins?
Source_Data_Required: SRC-006 (Detailed Customer Sales Register), SRC-007 (Customer Master), SRC-010 (SKU Costing Records)
Periods_Covered: Annual for 3 historical years (FY21, FY22, FY23) and LTM
Entities_Covered: Consolidated group and customer sales ledgers
Analytical_Method: Pareto 80/20 concentration analysis; customer profitability tiering; Herfindahl-Hirschman Index (HHI).
Detailed_Procedure: Sort customers by revenue descending; calculate cumulative revenue and gross profit %; calculate individual customer gross margin %; cross-reference customer credit ratings and contract expiration dates; test for margin leakage on large volume accounts.
Metrics_Produced: Top 5/10/20 Customer Concentration % (Revenue and GP), Customer Gross Margin Ranking, At-Risk Revenue Volume.
Common_Findings_Patterns: Top 5 customers account for 44.8% of revenue but only 36.2% of gross profit due to aggressive volume discounting; Customer #1 gross margin is 28.5% vs 38.0% company average.
Potential_Distortions: Affiliated related-party customer revenues lumped into third-party customer totals; one-time spot project work presented as recurring customer revenue.
Further_Investigative_Questions: Are top customer relationships governed by long-term Master Service Agreements (MSAs) or purchase orders? When do key contracts expire?
Required_Evidence: EVD-005 (Customer contract agreements, pricing schedules, sales ledger transaction extracts)
Source_References: FTI Consulting Commercial TAS; AICPA Customer Analytics Guide

Procedure_Name: Balance Sheet Working Capital Velocity & Turn Analysis (DSO, DIO, DPO)
Analytical_Objective: Examine historical working capital turnover metrics and detect cash flow friction or artificial supplier stretching.
Financial_Question_Investigated: How efficiently does the business turn working capital, and did the 9-day expansion in DSO drain operating cash in FY23?
Source_Data_Required: SRC-001 (Prepared TB Balance Sheet Accounts), ANA-001 (P&L Revenue and COGS)
Periods_Covered: Monthly and annual for 3 historical years (FY21-FY23) and LTM
Analytical_Method: Days Sales Outstanding (DSO = (AR / Revenue) * 365); Days Inventory Outstanding (DIO = (Inv / COGS) * 365); Days Payable Outstanding (DPO = (AP / COGS) * 365); Cash Conversion Cycle (CCC = DSO + DIO - DPO).
Detailed_Procedure: Calculate DSO, DIO, and DPO on a 12-month rolling and monthly countback basis; bridge Net Working Capital as % of revenue over time; identify whether liquidity is being supported by delaying vendor payments.
Metrics_Produced: DSO (Days), DIO (Days), DPO (Days), Cash Conversion Cycle (Days), NWC as % of Revenue.
Common_Findings_Patterns: Cash Conversion Cycle expanded from 68 days in FY21 to 81 days in FY23, driven by customer payment delays (+9 days DSO) and buffer inventory (+7 days DIO).
Potential_Distortions: Significant year-end unapplied cash or disputed vendor invoices distorting closing balance sheet balances; factoring of receivables off-balance sheet.
Further_Investigative_Questions: What are standard contractual payment terms with top customers and suppliers? Are there overdue receivables over 90 days?
Required_Evidence: EVD-006 (Detailed AR aging), EVD-007 (Detailed AP aging), EVD-008 (Perpetual inventory)
Expected_Analytical_Output: ANA-011 (Working Capital Velocity & Cash Conversion Cycle Workpaper)
Relevant_Business_Models: Distribution/Wholesale, Manufacturing (Adapted for SaaS via unbilled/deferred)
Downstream_Dependencies: WS07 (Target Working Capital Peg & Deficiency Analysis)
Source_References: Alvarez & Marsal Working Capital Practice; PwC TAS Working Capital Guide

Procedure_Name: Historical Cash Flow Conversion (EBITDA to OCF / FCF) Analysis
Analytical_Objective: Bridge historical reported EBITDA to Operating Cash Flow and Free Cash Flow to test earnings cash backing.
Financial_Question_Investigated: Do the company’s paper EBITDA profits actually convert into real distributable bank cash?
Source_Data_Required: REC-001 (Reconciled TB), REC-009 (Proof of Cash), ANA-001 (Income Statement), ANA-011 (Working Capital)
Periods_Covered: Annual for 3 historical years (FY21-FY23) and LTM
Analytical_Method: Indirect cash flow waterfall; Operating Cash Conversion Ratio = OCF / EBITDA; Free Cash Flow Conversion Ratio = FCF / EBITDA.
Detailed_Procedure: Start with reported Operating EBITDA; adjust for non-cash working capital changes (Delta AR, Delta Inv, Delta AP); subtract cash taxes and cash interest paid to arrive at Operating Cash Flow (OCF); subtract maintenance CapEx to arrive at Free Cash Flow; calculate conversion ratios.
Metrics_Produced: Operating Cash Flow ($), OCF / EBITDA Conversion %, Free Cash Flow ($), FCF / EBITDA Conversion %.
Common_Findings_Patterns: Cash conversion ratio dropped from 65.0% in FY21 to 54.3% in FY23; .52M of EBITDA was trapped in working capital and equipment CapEx.
Potential_Distortions: Capital leases and financing debt payments classified inconsistently in operating vs financing cash flows; unrecorded tax liabilities.
Further_Investigative_Questions: Why did cash conversion deteriorate in a growing business? What is the minimum cash required to maintain current plant operations?
Required_Evidence: EVD-009 (Direct bank statements, proof of cash reconciliations), EVD-011 (CapEx invoices)
Expected_Analytical_Output: ANA-012 (EBITDA to Cash Conversion Waterfall Workpaper)
Downstream_Dependencies: WS07 (Net Debt & Cash Flow Debt Service Capacity)
Source_References: Kroll Valuation & Diligence Practice; CFA Institute Corporate Finance

Procedure_Name: Capital Expenditure Trend Analysis (Growth vs. Maintenance CapEx)
Analytical_Objective: Bifurcate historical CapEx into non-discretionary maintenance expenditures and discretionary growth investments.
Financial_Question_Investigated: What is the true recurring maintenance CapEx required to support the business, and is depreciation representative of CapEx needs?
Source_Data_Required: SRC-016 (Fixed Asset Register), SRC-002 (GL Fixed Asset Additions), Vendor Invoices
Periods_Covered: Annual for 3 historical years (FY21-FY23) and LTM
Analytical_Method: Asset-by-asset categorization; CapEx-to-Depreciation ratio (CapEx / D&A); Maintenance CapEx as % of revenue.
Detailed_Procedure: Sample all fixed asset additions >; audit invoice descriptions; classify into Maintenance (repair parts, IT hardware, fleet replacement, routine tooling) vs Growth (new plant lines, facility expansion, new tech platforms); compare maintenance CapEx to annual depreciation.
Metrics_Produced: Maintenance CapEx ($), Growth CapEx ($), Maintenance CapEx % of Revenue, CapEx / Depreciation Ratio.
Common_Findings_Patterns: Maintenance CapEx averaged /yr (2.3% of revenue), while depreciation averaged /yr; management deferred routine fleet maintenance ahead of the transaction.
Potential_Distortions: Routine repairs and maintenance expensed in SG&A to depress EBITDA, or conversely, capitalized into fixed assets to artificially inflate EBITDA.
Further_Investigative_Questions: What equipment replacements are legally mandated or required within the next 18 months? What is the average age of plant machinery?
Required_Evidence: EVD-011 (Detailed FAR register, capital expenditure approval forms, vendor equipment invoices)
Downstream_Dependencies: WS05 (Maintenance CapEx adjustments for Unlevered Free Cash Flow valuation)
Source_References: PwC TAS CapEx Guide; Houlihan Lokey Private Equity Diligence

Procedure_Name: SaaS Recurring Revenue Waterfall, Churn, and Retention Analysis
Analytical_Objective: Analyze Annual Recurring Revenue (ARR), Monthly Recurring Revenue (MRR), gross retention, net retention, and churn.
Financial_Question_Investigated: Is historical SaaS growth driven by healthy existing customer expansion or aggressive marketing masking high churn?
Source_Data_Required: SRC-019 (SaaS Billing & Deferred Revenue Waterfall), SRC-020 (Customer Subscription Contracts)
Periods_Covered: Monthly for 36 months (cohorts) and 3 historical fiscal years
Analytical_Method: ARR Waterfall Bridge: Beg ARR + New ARR + Expansion ARR - Churned ARR - Contraction ARR = End ARR; Gross Revenue Retention (GRR); Net Revenue Retention (NRR).
Detailed_Procedure: Reconcile monthly subscription billing records; calculate GRR = (Beg ARR - Churn - Contraction) / Beg ARR; calculate NRR = (Beg ARR - Churn - Contraction + Expansion) / Beg ARR; track Logo Churn vs Dollar Churn; calculate Magic Number and CAC Payback Period.
Metrics_Produced: Ending ARR ($), MRR ($), Gross Revenue Retention % (GRR), Net Revenue Retention % (NRR), Logo Churn %, CAC Payback (Months).
Common_Findings_Patterns: NRR is 108% but GRR is only 84%, indicating that substantial gross customer churn (-16%/yr) is being masked by large upsells to two enterprise accounts.
Potential_Distortions: One-time implementation setup fees or professional services included in ARR; multi-year contracts billed upfront treated as in-period recurring revenue.
Further_Investigative_Questions: What is customer churn by cohort? Are customer contract renewal rates declining in specific product modules?
Required_Evidence: EVD-014 (Stripe/Chargebee billing waterfall reports, customer Master Service Agreements)
Expected_Analytical_Output: ANA-014 (SaaS ARR Waterfall & Cohort Retention Workpaper)
Downstream_Dependencies: WS06 (SaaS Recurring Revenue Quality & Churn Diligence)
Source_References: Bessemer SaaS Metrics Framework; Key Capital SaaS Due Diligence
